messages:
samir: FYI customer redwood-corp reported tool_result mapping getting mixed up when using parallel tool calls in hosted API v2. They see tool outputs attributed to the wrong tool id. Correlation: 01H2X9ZQ8G7T3. SDK: js 0.9.3. Severity: customer blocking.

olivia: got it. can you paste a minimal repro? i have a dev env free to test.

samir: customer provided this request payload (sanitized):
```json
{
  \"model\": \"rwd-infer-1\",
  \"input\": \"Get latest order for user 123 and search docs for pricing of widget X\",
  \"tools\": [
    {\"name\": \"db_query\", \"args\": {\"user_id\": 123}},
    {\"name\": \"web_search\", \"args\": {\"query\": \"widget X pricing\"}}
  ],
  \"tools_parallel\": true,
  \"return_tool_results\": true
}
```
Responses sometimes look like: model returns tool_result[0] = web_search result, tool_result[1] = db row, but tool names flipped in the final structured output.

alex_k: reproduced locally with SDK 0.9.3 and hosted-stub. i instrumented the client -> server payloads. server receives two tool_call entries with tool_call_id: c1 and c2. both tool executions complete at slightly different times. final response mapping code seems to reassemble results by array index instead of tool_call_id. logs: 
```
[2026-02-12T15:02:10.123Z] REQUEST id=01H2X9ZQ8G7T3 tool_call_id=c1 tool=db_query
[2026-02-12T15:02:10.127Z] REQUEST id=01H2X9ZQ8G7T3 tool_call_id=c2 tool=web_search
[2026-02-12T15:02:10.230Z] TOOL_DONE id=01H2X9ZQ8G7T3 tool_call_id=c2 result_id=r2
[2026-02-12T15:02:10.245Z] TOOL_DONE id=01H2X9ZQ8G7T3 tool_call_id=c1 result_id=r1
[2026-02-12T15:02:10.300Z] ASSEMBLE_RESPONSE id=01H2X9ZQ8G7T3 mapping_by_index true mapped_results=[r1,r2]
```
You can see r2 completed first but assembly used original index ordering.

maya: that looks like a race in the reassembly path. if assembly ignores tool_call_id -> index-based merge yields swapped mapping when completions are out-of-order.

ryan: is there any PII/billing risk? customer said results were used downstream in structured inserts. risk of mismatched row + external doc could be data integrity / privacy depending on tool outputs. escalate.

triage: opened INC-2026-248 for redwood-corp. severity P1 (data integrity/high customer impact). assigned to eng-runtime and eng-ml.

eng-bot: INC-2026-248 created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-248. linked to backlog task RWD-TOOLS-913.

olivia: quick repro script i ran (node):
```js
const client = require('@redwood/inference-js')
await client.predict({
  model: 'rwd-infer-1',
  input: '...same as above...',
  tools: [
    {name: 'db_query', args: {user_id:123}},
    {name: 'web_search', args: {query: 'widget X pricing'}}
  ],
  tools_parallel: true
})
```
i see swapped mapping ~3/10 runs locally.

samir: customer logs show ~7% of multi-tool calls affected in production region us-west-2 over last 24h. latency spike correlated: median tool latency higher and variance bigger -> more out-of-order completions.

alex_k: short-term mitigation options: 1) force sequential tool execution for the customer (tools_parallel=false) - immediate but impacts latency, 2) in gateway, reassemble by tool_call_id if present (quick patch), 3) client-side: add explicit call_id and rely on server mapping (but server should still be correct).

maya: engineering note: the runtime currently stores tool results in a vector and appends as completions arrive, then zips with original tool list by index at the end path. fix: use a dict keyed by tool_call_id and reconstruct in original request order by looking up that id. low risk change but must add tests for OOO completions and streaming.

ryan: propose customer-facing mitigation: enable sequential mode for redwood-corp and roll a hotfix to map by tool_call_id. ask legal/CS if we need to notify about data integrity.

triage: applied mitigation: sequential mode enabled on their tenant (account:redwood-corp) at 15:12 UTC. CS notified.

eng-bot: patch PR created RWD-TOOLS-913 PR#459 by alex_k. CI green, added unit tests for OOO completions. target canary deploy tomorrow 08:00 UTC.

samir: customer confirmed reduced failures after sequential mode. they accept canary schedule but want ETA for permanent fix.

alex_k: ETA for fix + rollout: 72h to get through canary -> staged -> prod. will keep updates in INC ticket.

maya: note for postmortem: add stress test with injected latency to each tool to force reordering and ensure mapping invariants.

samir: thanks all. marking thread for follow-up once PR merged. customer id and logs attached in the INC-2026-248 ticket. :white_check_mark:
